    28	private theorem opFamilyDistSq_self_mul_eq_one_sub_overlap
    29	    {X α ι : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    30	    (μ : Distribution X) (A : X → Measurement α ι) (B : X → α → Op ι)
    31	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (hμ : μ.IsProbability) (hψ : ‖ψ‖ = 1)
    32	    (hA : ∀ x, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (A x))
    33	    (hB : ∀ x a, IsProj (B x a))
    34	    (hAB : ∀ x a, Commute ((A x).effect a) (B x a)) :
    35	    opFamilyDistSq μ (fun x a => (A x).effect a)
    36	        (fun x a => (A x).effect a * B x a) ψ =
    37	      1 - avgOver μ (fun x =>
    38	        ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * B x a)) := by
    39	  unfold opFamilyDistSq
    40	  calc
    41	    avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a,
    42	        ‖applyOperatorToState ((A x).effect a - (A x).effect a * B x a) ψ‖ ^ 2) =
    43	        avgOver μ (fun x => 1 -
    44	          ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * B x a)) := by
    45	      refine avgOver_congr _ _ _ fun x => ?_
    46	      rw [← sum_stateQForm_effect_eq_one (A x) ψ hψ,
    47	        ← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
    48	      refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
    49	      have hcomm : Commute ((A x).effect a) (1 - B x a) :=
    50	        (Commute.one_right _).sub_right (hAB x a)
    51	      have hprod : IsProj ((A x).effect a * (1 - B x a)) :=
    52	        (hA x a).mul (hB x a).one_sub hcomm
    53	      rw [show (A x).effect a - (A x).effect a * B x a =
    54	          (A x).effect a * (1 - B x a) by rw [mul_sub, mul_one]]
    55	      rw [norm_applyOperatorToState_sq_eq_stateQForm,
    56	        hprod.isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.eq, hprod.isIdempotentElem.eq]
    57	      simp [stateQForm, applyOperatorToState, mul_sub]
    58	    _ = _ := by
    59	      rw [avgOver_sub, avgOver_const_of_isProbability μ hμ]
    60	
    61	/-- The overlap of the constructed X-Z-X line measurement with the expanded
    62	X-point effect selected by the X-line answer. -/
    63	def concreteXPointOverlap {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ}
    64	    (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
    65	    (w : (LineDesc P.toLdParams × LineDesc P.toLdParams) ×
    66	      (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)) : ℝ :=
    67	  ∑ fX, ∑ fZ, stateQForm S.psiHat
    68	    (S.place .AA'
    69	        ((S.combinedLineMeasurement Placement.AA'.side w.1.1 w.1.2).effect
    70	          (fX, fZ)) *
    71	      S.place .BA''
    72	        (S.expPointEffectAtLineAnswer Placement.BA''.side .X w.1.1 w.2 fX))
    73	
    74	private theorem concreteXPointOverlap_eq_linePointOverlap
    75	    {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ} (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
    76	    (lineX lineZ : LineDesc P.toLdParams) (x : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
    77	    concreteXPointOverlap S ((lineX, lineZ), x) =
    78	      ∑ fX, stateQForm S.psiHat
    79	        (S.place .AA'
    80	            ((S.lineMeasExp Placement.AA'.side .X lineX).effect fX) *
    81	          S.place .BA''
    82	            (S.expPointEffectAtLineAnswer Placement.BA''.side .X lineX x fX)) := by
    83	  classical
    84	  unfold concreteXPointOverlap
    85	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun fX _ => ?_
    86	  rw [← DistanceCalculus.stateQForm_finset_sum, ← Finset.sum_mul,
    87	    ← S.place_finset_sum, S.combinedLineMeasurement_sum_Z]
    88	
    89	private theorem concreteXPointOverlap_restricted_deficit_le
    90	    (C : ℝ)
    91	    (hC : 0 ≤ C)
    92	    (hline : ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ) (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
    93	      (p₁ p₂ : Placement), p₁.IsOpposite p₂ → ∀ W : PauliKind,
    94	      opFamilyDistSq (linePointDist P.toLdParams)
    95	        (fun sample f => S.place p₁
    96	          ((S.lineMeasExp p₁.side W sample.1).effect f))
    97	        (fun sample f =>
    98	          S.place p₁ ((S.lineMeasExp p₁.side W sample.1).effect f) *
    99	            S.place p₂ (S.expPointEffectAtLineAnswer p₂.side W
   100	              sample.1 sample.2 f))
   101	        S.psiHat ≤ C * deltaLine ε)
   102	    (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ) (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   103	    (kind : LineKind) (i j : Fin P.m) :
   104	    1 - avgOver (Distribution.prod (restrictedLinePointDist P kind i)
   105	        (restrictedLinePointDist P kind j))
   106	      (fun w => concreteXPointOverlap S ((w.1.1, w.2.1), w.1.2)) ≤
   107	      2 * C * (P.m : ℝ) ^ 2 * deltaLine ε := by
   108	  classical
   109	  let μX := restrictedLinePointDist P kind i
   110	  let μZ := restrictedLinePointDist P kind j
   111	  have hμX : μX.IsProbability := restrictedLinePointDist_isProbability P kind i
   112	  have hμZ : μZ.IsProbability := restrictedLinePointDist_isProbability P kind j
   113	  have hcollapse : avgOver (Distribution.prod μX μZ)
   114	      (fun w => concreteXPointOverlap S ((w.1.1, w.2.1), w.1.2)) =
   115	      avgOver μX (fun w => ∑ fX, stateQForm S.psiHat
   116	        (S.place .AA'
   117	            ((S.lineMeasExp Placement.AA'.side .X w.1).effect fX) *
   118	          S.place .BA''
   119	            (S.expPointEffectAtLineAnswer Placement.BA''.side .X w.1 w.2 fX))) := by
   120	    rw [avgOver_prod]
   121	    refine avgOver_congr _ _ _ fun wX => ?_
   122	    calc
   123	      avgOver μZ (fun wZ =>
   124	          concreteXPointOverlap S ((wX.1, wZ.1), wX.2)) =
   125	          avgOver μZ (fun _ => ∑ fX, stateQForm S.psiHat
   126	            (S.place .AA'
   127	                ((S.lineMeasExp Placement.AA'.side .X wX.1).effect fX) *
   128	              S.place .BA'' (S.expPointEffectAtLineAnswer
   129	                Placement.BA''.side .X wX.1 wX.2 fX))) := by
   130	        refine avgOver_congr _ _ _ fun wZ => ?_
   131	        exact concreteXPointOverlap_eq_linePointOverlap S wX.1 wZ.1 wX.2
   132	      _ = _ := avgOver_const_of_isProbability μZ hμZ _
   133	  rw [hcollapse]
   134	  let A : (LineDesc P.toLdParams × (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)) →
   135	      Measurement (DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d))
   136	        (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) := fun w =>
   137	    S.placedMeasurement .AA' (S.lineMeasExp Placement.AA'.side .X w.1)
   138	  let B : (LineDesc P.toLdParams × (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)) →
   139	      DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d) →
   140	        Op (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) := fun w f =>
   141	    S.place .BA'' (S.expPointEffectAtLineAnswer Placement.BA''.side .X w.1 w.2 f)
   142	  change 1 - avgOver μX (fun w => ∑ f,
   143	      stateQForm S.psiHat ((A w).effect f * B w f)) ≤ _
   144	  rw [← opFamilyDistSq_self_mul_eq_one_sub_overlap μX A B S.psiHat hμX
   145	    S.psiHat_norm]
   146	  · calc
   147	      opFamilyDistSq μX (fun w f => (A w).effect f)
   148	          (fun w f => (A w).effect f * B w f) S.psiHat ≤
   149	          2 * (P.m : ℝ) * opFamilyDistSq (linePointDist P.toLdParams)
   150	            (fun w f => (A w).effect f)
   151	            (fun w f => (A w).effect f * B w f) S.psiHat := by
   152	        exact avgOver_restrictedLinePointDist_le _
   153	          (fun w => Finset.sum_nonneg fun f _ => sq_nonneg _) kind i
   154	      _ ≤ 2 * (P.m : ℝ) * (C * deltaLine ε) := by
   155	        exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hline P ε S .AA' .BA'' trivial .X)
   156	          (by positivity)
   157	      _ ≤ 2 * C * (P.m : ℝ) ^ 2 * deltaLine ε := by
   158	        have hm : (1 : ℝ) ≤ (P.m : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast P.one_le_m
   159	        have hCδ : 0 ≤ C * deltaLine ε := by
   160	          exact mul_nonneg hC (Real.sqrt_nonneg _)
   161	        have hstep := mul_nonneg (sub_nonneg.mpr hm) hCδ
   162	        nlinarith
   163	  · intro w
   164	    exact S.placedMeasurement_isProjective .AA' _
   165	      (S.lineMeasExp_isProjective .alice .X w.1)
   166	  · intro w f
   167	    dsimp only [B]
   168	    rw [← S.pointMeasExpOption_effect_evalOpt]
   169	    exact S.place_isProj .BA''
   170	      (S.pointMeasExpOption_isProj Placement.BA''.side .X w.2 _)
   171	  · intro w f
   172	    exact S.place_comm .AA' .BA'' trivial _ _
   173	
   174	/-- The concrete X overlap over the directly indexed subline law has deficit at most a
   175	universal constant times `m² * deltaLine ε`. This is the restricted-line
   176	estimate used after Cauchy--Schwarz in `lem:claim-17-2`, paper
   177	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1168-1201`.
   178	
   179	**Scope restriction:** `SubLineWitness` describes the directly indexed law.
   180	Transport to the source law remains open as recorded in
   181	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`. This real deficit estimate
   182	does not itself prove the complex scalar comparison; see issue #474 and
   183	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_subline-claims-line-marginal.tex`. -/

   185	    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧
   186	      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ)
   187	        (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (sublines : SubLineWitness P),
   188	        1 - avgOver sublines.D (fun sample =>
   189	          avgOver (uniformDistribution (DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd))
   190	            (fun t => concreteXPointOverlap S
   191	              (sample.2, projX (directPointToPauli P
   192	                (sample.1.base + t • sample.1.direction))))) ≤
   193	          C * (P.m : ℝ) ^ 2 * deltaLine ε := by
   194	  obtain ⟨C, hC, hline⟩ := expLine_point_cons
   195	  refine ⟨2 * C, by positivity, ?_⟩
   196	  intro P ε S sublines
   197	  obtain ⟨components, hcomp, hmix⟩ :=
   198	    sublines.exists_avgOver_X_eq_mixture P (concreteXPointOverlap S)

   200	  have hsplit : avgOver components (fun c => 1 -
   201	      avgOver (Distribution.prod (restrictedLinePointDist P c.1 c.2.1)
   202	        (restrictedLinePointDist P c.1 c.2.2))
   203	        (fun w => concreteXPointOverlap S ((w.1.1, w.2.1), w.1.2))) =
   204	      1 - avgOver components (fun c =>
   205	        avgOver (Distribution.prod (restrictedLinePointDist P c.1 c.2.1)
   206	          (restrictedLinePointDist P c.1 c.2.2))
   207	          (fun w => concreteXPointOverlap S ((w.1.1, w.2.1), w.1.2))) := by
   208	    rw [avgOver_sub, avgOver_const_of_isProbability components hcomp]
   209	  rw [← hsplit]
   210	  calc
   211	    _ ≤ avgOver components (fun _ =>
   212	        2 * C * (P.m : ℝ) ^ 2 * deltaLine ε) := by
   213	      refine avgOver_mono _ _ _ fun c => ?_
   214	      exact concreteXPointOverlap_restricted_deficit_le C (by linarith) hline P ε S

   216	    _ = _ := avgOver_const_of_isProbability components hcomp _
   217

     4	/-!
     5	# The ordered point product on a single placement
     6	
     7	The consistency guarantees carried by the joint point measurement compare it
     8	with the ordered `Z`-then-`X` product across a pair of opposite placements.
     9	The scalar estimates used to combine the two Pauli bases instead need the two
    10	families on one placement.  This module obtains that form by inserting the
    11	joint measurement on the opposite placement and applying the squared-distance
    12	triangle inequality twice.
    13	
    14	## References
    15	
    16	The statement is `lem:qld-4-10-same-placement` in
    17	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex`; it restates the ordered
    18	`Z`-then-`X` display of `lem:qld-4-10`, paper
    19	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:689-709`.
    20	-/

    23	
    24	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    25	
    26	open MIPStarRE.LDT hiding Measurement
    27	open MIPStarRE.Quantum

    29	noncomputable section

    31	/-- Every placement has an opposite placement, and the relation is symmetric
    32	between the two members of each pair. -/
    33	theorem Placement.exists_isOpposite (p : Placement) :
    34	    ∃ q : Placement, p.IsOpposite q ∧ q.IsOpposite p := by
    35	  cases p with
    36	  | AA' => exact ⟨.BA'', trivial, trivial⟩
    37	  | BA'' => exact ⟨.AA', trivial, trivial⟩
    38	  | BB' => exact ⟨.AB'', trivial, trivial⟩
    39	  | AB'' => exact ⟨.BB', trivial, trivial⟩
    40	
    41	/-- On a single placement, the joint point measurement is close to the ordered
    42	`Z`-then-`X` point product, with inflation factor four. -/
    43	theorem CombinedPointsWitness.orderedZX_dist_le {P : AdmissibleParams}
    44	    {ε δ : ℝ} {S : ProjectiveSetting P ε}
    45	    (points : CombinedPointsWitness S δ) (p : Placement) :
    46	    opFamilyDistSq
    47	        (uniformDistribution
    48	          ((Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) × (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)))
    49	        (fun xz ab => S.place p ((points.Q p.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))
    50	        (fun xz ab => S.place p
    51	          ((S.pointMeasExp p.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2 *
    52	            (S.pointMeasExp p.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1))
    53	        S.psiHat ≤ 4 * δ := by
    54	  obtain ⟨q, hpq, hqp⟩ := p.exists_isOpposite
    55	  have htri := opFamilyDistSq_le_of_le_of_le
    56	    (uniformDistribution
    57	      ((Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) × (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)))
    58	    (fun xz ab => S.place p ((points.Q p.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))
    59	    (fun xz ab => S.place q ((points.Q q.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))
    60	    (fun xz ab => S.place p
    61	      ((S.pointMeasExp p.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2 *
    62	        (S.pointMeasExp p.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1))
    63	    S.psiHat δ δ (points.self_consistent p q hpq)
    64	    (points.consistent_ZX q p hqp)
    65	  linarith
    66	
    67	end

     4	/-!
     5	# Replacing one factor of a measurement-weighted overlap
     6	
     7	The scalar estimates used to combine the two Pauli bases compare averaged
     8	overlaps whose left factor is one complete measurement and whose right factors
     9	are operator families at small state-dependent distance.  This module records
    10	the corresponding Cauchy--Schwarz estimate.  The right-hand families are
    11	arbitrary, so the estimate covers an ordered product of point effects, which
    12	is not itself a measurement.
    13	
    14	## References
    15	
    16	The estimate is `lem:overlap-gap-distance` in
    17	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex`; it is the Cauchy--Schwarz
    18	step at paper
    19	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1147-1166`.
    20	-/
    21	
    22	open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
    23	
    24	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    25	
    26	open MIPStarRE.LDT hiding Measurement
    27	open MIPStarRE.Quantum MIPStarRE.QPBT.DistanceCalculus
    28	
    29	/-- Replacing one operator family inside an overlap weighted on the left by a
    30	complete measurement changes the average by at most the square root of the
    31	state-dependent squared distance between the two families. -/
    32	theorem abs_overlap_gap_le_sqrt_of_opFamilyDistSq {X α ι : Type*}
    33	    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    34	    (μ : Distribution X) (A : X → Measurement α ι) (B C : X → α → Op ι)
    35	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (hμ : μ.IsProbability) (hψ : ‖ψ‖ = 1)
    36	    (ζ : ℝ) (hBC : opFamilyDistSq μ B C ψ ≤ ζ) :
    37	    |avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a : α, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * B x a)) -
    38	        avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a : α, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * C x a))| ≤
    39	      Real.sqrt ζ := by
    40	  classical
    41	  have hnorm_sq : ∀ M : Op ι,
    42	      ‖applyOperatorToState M ψ‖ ^ 2 = stateQForm ψ (Mᴴ * M) := by
    43	    intro M
    44	    rw [@norm_sq_eq_re_inner ℂ]
    45	    unfold stateQForm applyOperatorToState

   144	/-! ## The Cauchy--Schwarz inequality weighted by a positive operator -/
   145	
   146	/-- For a positive operator `A`, the sesquilinear form `⟨u, A v⟩` satisfies the
   147	Cauchy--Schwarz inequality with the two diagonal values `⟨u, A u⟩` and
   148	`⟨v, A v⟩`.  This is the inequality behind the Cauchy--Schwarz steps of the
   149	proofs of `lem:claim-17-2` and `lem:claim-17-3`, in which both factors carry
   150	the square root of the line effect, paper
   151	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1168-1209`. -/
   152	theorem norm_inner_applyOperatorToState_le_sqrt_mul_sqrt {ι : Type*}
   153	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {A : Op ι} (hA : 0 ≤ A)
   154	    (u v : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
   155	    ‖inner ℂ u (applyOperatorToState A v)‖ ≤
   156	      Real.sqrt (inner ℂ u (applyOperatorToState A u)).re *
   157	        Real.sqrt (inner ℂ v (applyOperatorToState A v)).re := by
   158	  set R : Op ι := CFC.sqrt A with hR
   159	  have hRnonneg : 0 ≤ R := CFC.sqrt_nonneg A
   160	  have hRR : R * R = A := CFC.sqrt_mul_sqrt_self A hA
   161	  have hRherm : Rᴴ = R :=
   162	    (Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mp hRnonneg).isHermitian.eq
   163	  have hadjoint : (Matrix.toEuclideanLin R).adjoint = Matrix.toEuclideanLin R := by
   164	    rw [← Matrix.toEuclideanLin_conjTranspose_eq_adjoint, hRherm]
   165	  have hsplit : ∀ w z : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι,
   166	      inner ℂ w (applyOperatorToState A z) =
   167	        inner ℂ (applyOperatorToState R w) (applyOperatorToState R z) := by
   168	    intro w z
   169	    have h := LinearMap.adjoint_inner_right (Matrix.toEuclideanLin R) w
   170	      (Matrix.toEuclideanLin R z)
   171	    rw [hadjoint] at h
   172	    rw [← hRR, applyOperatorToState_mul]
   173	    exact h
   174	  have hnorm : ∀ w : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι,
   175	      ‖applyOperatorToState R w‖ =
   176	        Real.sqrt (inner ℂ w (applyOperatorToState A w)).re := by
   177	    intro w
   178	    have h2 : ‖applyOperatorToState R w‖ ^ 2 =
   179	        (inner ℂ (applyOperatorToState R w) (applyOperatorToState R w)).re := by
   180	      rw [@norm_sq_eq_re_inner ℂ]
   181	      rfl
   182	    rw [hsplit, ← h2, Real.sqrt_sq (norm_nonneg _)]
   183	  rw [hsplit, ← hnorm, ← hnorm]
   184	  exact norm_inner_le_norm _ _

   186	/-- The sum over outcomes of the real parts of `⟨u a, A a (v a)⟩`, for
   187	positive weights `A a`, is bounded by the product of the square roots of the
   188	two diagonal sums. -/
   189	theorem abs_sum_re_inner_le_sqrt_mul_sqrt {α ι : Type*} [Fintype α]
   190	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : α → Op ι) (hA : ∀ a, 0 ≤ A a)
   191	    (u v : α → EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
   192	    |∑ a, (inner ℂ (u a) (applyOperatorToState (A a) (v a))).re| ≤
   193	      Real.sqrt (∑ a, (inner ℂ (u a) (applyOperatorToState (A a) (u a))).re) *
   194	        Real.sqrt (∑ a, (inner ℂ (v a) (applyOperatorToState (A a) (v a))).re) := by
   195	  have hu : ∀ a, 0 ≤ (inner ℂ (u a) (applyOperatorToState (A a) (u a))).re :=
   196	    fun a => stateQForm_nonneg (u a) (hA a)
   197	  have hv : ∀ a, 0 ≤ (inner ℂ (v a) (applyOperatorToState (A a) (v a))).re :=
   198	    fun a => stateQForm_nonneg (v a) (hA a)
   199	  calc
   200	    |∑ a, (inner ℂ (u a) (applyOperatorToState (A a) (v a))).re|
   201	        ≤ ∑ a, |(inner ℂ (u a) (applyOperatorToState (A a) (v a))).re| :=
   202	      Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs _ _
   203	    _ ≤ ∑ a, Real.sqrt (inner ℂ (u a) (applyOperatorToState (A a) (u a))).re *
   204	          Real.sqrt (inner ℂ (v a) (applyOperatorToState (A a) (v a))).re := by
   205	      refine Finset.sum_le_sum fun a _ => ?_
   206	      exact (Complex.abs_re_le_norm _).trans
   207	        (norm_inner_applyOperatorToState_le_sqrt_mul_sqrt (hA a) (u a) (v a))
   208	    _ ≤ Real.sqrt (∑ a,
   209	            Real.sqrt (inner ℂ (u a) (applyOperatorToState (A a) (u a))).re ^ 2) *
   210	          Real.sqrt (∑ a,
   211	            Real.sqrt (inner ℂ (v a) (applyOperatorToState (A a) (v a))).re ^ 2) :=
   212	      Real.sum_mul_le_sqrt_mul_sqrt _ _ _
   213	    _ = _ := by
   214	      rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => Real.sq_sqrt (hu a),
   215	        Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => Real.sq_sqrt (hv a)]
   216	
   217	/-- The averaged form of the preceding estimate: the average over a
   218	distribution of the outcome sums of `Re ⟨u, A v⟩` is bounded by the product of
   219	the square roots of the two averaged diagonal sums. -/
   220	theorem abs_avgOver_sum_re_inner_le_sqrt_mul_sqrt {X α ι : Type*} [Fintype α]
   221	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (μ : Distribution X) (A : X → α → Op ι)
   222	    (hA : ∀ x a, 0 ≤ A x a) (u v : X → α → EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
   223	    |avgOver μ (fun x =>
   224	        ∑ a, (inner ℂ (u x a) (applyOperatorToState (A x a) (v x a))).re)| ≤
   225	      Real.sqrt (avgOver μ (fun x =>
   226	          ∑ a, (inner ℂ (u x a) (applyOperatorToState (A x a) (u x a))).re)) *
   227	        Real.sqrt (avgOver μ (fun x =>
   228	          ∑ a, (inner ℂ (v x a) (applyOperatorToState (A x a) (v x a))).re)) := by
   229	  set f : X → ℝ := fun x =>
   230	    ∑ a, (inner ℂ (u x a) (applyOperatorToState (A x a) (v x a))).re with hf
   231	  set g : X → ℝ := fun x =>
   232	    ∑ a, (inner ℂ (u x a) (applyOperatorToState (A x a) (u x a))).re with hg
   233	  set h : X → ℝ := fun x =>
   234	    ∑ a, (inner ℂ (v x a) (applyOperatorToState (A x a) (v x a))).re with hh
   235	  have hg0 : ∀ x, 0 ≤ g x := fun x =>
   236	    Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => stateQForm_nonneg (u x a) (hA x a)
   237	  have hh0 : ∀ x, 0 ≤ h x := fun x =>
   238	    Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => stateQForm_nonneg (v x a) (hA x a)
   239	  have hpoint : ∀ x, |f x| ≤ Real.sqrt (g x) * Real.sqrt (h x) := fun x =>
   240	    abs_sum_re_inner_le_sqrt_mul_sqrt (A x) (hA x) (u x) (v x)
   241	  unfold avgOver
   242	  calc
   243	    |∑ x ∈ μ.support, μ.weight x * f x|
   244	        ≤ ∑ x ∈ μ.support, |μ.weight x * f x| := Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs _ _
   245	    _ = ∑ x ∈ μ.support, μ.weight x * |f x| := by
   246	      refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun x _ => ?_
   247	      rw [abs_mul, abs_of_nonneg (μ.nonnegative x)]
   248	    _ ≤ ∑ x ∈ μ.support, μ.weight x * (Real.sqrt (g x) * Real.sqrt (h x)) :=
   249	      Finset.sum_le_sum fun x _ =>
   250	        mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hpoint x) (μ.nonnegative x)
   251	    _ = ∑ x ∈ μ.support,
   252	          Real.sqrt (μ.weight x * g x) * Real.sqrt (μ.weight x * h x) := by
   253	      refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun x _ => ?_
   254	      rw [Real.sqrt_mul (μ.nonnegative x), Real.sqrt_mul (μ.nonnegative x),
   255	        show Real.sqrt (μ.weight x) * Real.sqrt (g x) *
   256	            (Real.sqrt (μ.weight x) * Real.sqrt (h x)) =
   257	          Real.sqrt (μ.weight x) * Real.sqrt (μ.weight x) *
   258	            (Real.sqrt (g x) * Real.sqrt (h x)) by ring,
   259	        Real.mul_self_sqrt (μ.nonnegative x)]
   260	    _ ≤ Real.sqrt (∑ x ∈ μ.support, Real.sqrt (μ.weight x * g x) ^ 2) *
   261	          Real.sqrt (∑ x ∈ μ.support, Real.sqrt (μ.weight x * h x) ^ 2) :=
   262	      Real.sum_mul_le_sqrt_mul_sqrt _ _ _
   263	    _ = _ := by
   264	      rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl fun x _ =>
   265	          Real.sq_sqrt (mul_nonneg (μ.nonnegative x) (hg0 x)),
   266	        Finset.sum_congr rfl fun x _ =>
   267	          Real.sq_sqrt (mul_nonneg (μ.nonnegative x) (hh0 x))]

   269	/-! ## Quadratic forms against projections -/
   270	
   271	/-- The real quadratic form is invariant under the conjugate transpose. -/
   272	theorem stateQForm_conjTranspose {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   273	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (M : Op ι) :
   274	    stateQForm ψ Mᴴ = stateQForm ψ M := by
   275	  unfold stateQForm
   276	  change (inner ℂ ψ (Matrix.toEuclideanLin Mᴴ ψ)).re =
   277	    (inner ℂ ψ (Matrix.toEuclideanLin M ψ)).re
   278	  rw [Matrix.toEuclideanLin_conjTranspose_eq_adjoint, LinearMap.adjoint_inner_right,
   279	    ← inner_conj_symm, Complex.conj_re]

   281	/-- For a projection `B` commuting with `A`, the quadratic form of `A` in
   282	`B ψ` is the quadratic form of `A B` in `ψ`. -/
   283	theorem stateQForm_applyOperatorToState_eq_of_isProj {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
   284	    [DecidableEq ι] (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) {A B : Op ι} (hB : IsProj B)
   285	    (hAB : Commute A B) :
   286	    stateQForm (applyOperatorToState B ψ) A = stateQForm ψ (A * B) := by
   287	  rw [← stateQForm_conjTranspose_mul_mul, hB.isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.eq,
   288	    ← hAB.eq, mul_assoc, hB.isIdempotentElem.eq]
   289	
   290	/-- The quadratic form of an operator bounded by the identity is bounded by
   291	the squared norm of the vector. -/
   292	theorem stateQForm_le_norm_sq_of_le_one {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   293	    (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) {A : Op ι} (hA : A ≤ 1) :
   294	    stateQForm v A ≤ ‖v‖ ^ 2 := by
   295	  rw [← stateQForm_one]
   296	  exact quadratic_form_mono hA v

   298	/-- The effects of a complete measurement have total quadratic form one on a
   299	unit vector. -/
   300	theorem sum_stateQForm_effect_eq_one {α ι : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype ι]
   301	    [DecidableEq ι] (A : Measurement α ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι)
   302	    (hψ : ‖ψ‖ = 1) :
   303	    (∑ a : α, stateQForm ψ (A.effect a)) = 1 := by
   304	  calc
   305	    (∑ a : α, stateQForm ψ (A.effect a)) =
   306	        stateQForm ψ (∑ a : α, A.effect a) := by
   307	      simp [stateQForm, applyOperatorToState]
   308	    _ = stateQForm ψ 1 := by rw [A.sum_eq_one]
   309	    _ = 1 := by rw [stateQForm_one, hψ, one_pow]

   311	/-- Weighting a complete measurement by commuting projections cannot exceed
   312	the total mass one. -/
   313	theorem avgOver_sum_stateQForm_mul_le_one {X α ι : Type*} [Fintype α]
   314	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (μ : Distribution X) (A : X → Measurement α ι)
   315	    (C : X → α → Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (hμ : μ.IsProbability)
   316	    (hψ : ‖ψ‖ = 1) (hC : ∀ x a, IsProj (C x a))
   317	    (hAC : ∀ x a, Commute ((A x).effect a) (C x a)) :
   318	    avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * C x a)) ≤ 1 := by
   319	  have hpt : ∀ x, (∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * C x a)) ≤ 1 := by
   320	    intro x
   321	    calc
   322	      (∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * C x a)) ≤
   323	          ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a) := by
   324	        refine Finset.sum_le_sum fun a _ => ?_
   325	        have h1 : stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * (1 - C x a)) =

   327	              stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * C x a) := by

   329	        have h2 : 0 ≤ stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * (1 - C x a)) := by

   332	          exact stateQForm_nonneg _ ((A x).pos a)

   334	      _ = 1 := sum_stateQForm_effect_eq_one (A x) ψ hψ

   336	    avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * C x a)) ≤
   337	        avgOver μ (fun _ => 1) := avgOver_mono μ _ _ hpt
   338	    _ = 1 := avgOver_const_of_isProbability μ hμ 1

   340	/-! ## Replacing a factor under the weight of a measurement -/
   341	
   342	/-- Cauchy--Schwarz with the measurement as weight: for projections `B`
   343	commuting with the effects of `A`, the averaged overlap of `A` against the
   344	product `B C` is bounded by the square roots of the averaged overlap of `A`
   345	against `B` and of the averaged quadratic form of `A` in `C ψ`.  This is the
   346	Cauchy--Schwarz step of the proofs of `lem:claim-17-2` and `lem:claim-17-3`,
   347	paper `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1168-1209`. -/
   348	theorem abs_avgOver_sum_stateQForm_mul_mul_le_sqrt_mul_sqrt {X α ι : Type*}

   350	    (A : X → Measurement α ι) (B C : X → α → Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι)
   351	    (hB : ∀ x a, IsProj (B x a))
   352	    (hAB : ∀ x a, Commute ((A x).effect a) (B x a)) :
   353	    |avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * (B x a * C x a)))| ≤
   354	      Real.sqrt (avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * B x a))) *
   355	        Real.sqrt (avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a,
   356	          stateQForm (applyOperatorToState (C x a) ψ) ((A x).effect a))) := by
   357	  have hrw : ∀ x a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * (B x a * C x a)) =
   358	      (inner ℂ (applyOperatorToState (B x a) ψ)
   359	        (applyOperatorToState ((A x).effect a)
   360	          (applyOperatorToState (C x a) ψ))).re := by
   361	    intro x a
   362	    unfold stateQForm
   363	    rw [← mul_assoc, (hAB x a).eq, mul_assoc, applyOperatorToState_mul,
   364	      applyOperatorToState_mul]
   365	    congr 1
   366	    have hadj : (Matrix.toEuclideanLin (B x a)).adjoint =
   367	        Matrix.toEuclideanLin (B x a) := by
   368	      rw [← Matrix.toEuclideanLin_conjTranspose_eq_adjoint,
   369	        (hB x a).isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.eq]
   370	    have h := LinearMap.adjoint_inner_right (Matrix.toEuclideanLin (B x a)) ψ
   371	      (applyOperatorToState ((A x).effect a) (applyOperatorToState (C x a) ψ))
   372	    rw [hadj] at h
   373	    exact h
   374	  have hleft : (fun x => ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * B x a)) =
   375	      fun x => ∑ a, (inner ℂ (applyOperatorToState (B x a) ψ)
   376	        (applyOperatorToState ((A x).effect a)
   377	          (applyOperatorToState (B x a) ψ))).re :=
   378	    funext fun x => Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ =>
   379	      (stateQForm_applyOperatorToState_eq_of_isProj ψ (hB x a) (hAB x a)).symm
   380	  have hmain : (fun x => ∑ a, stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * (B x a * C x a))) =
   381	      fun x => ∑ a, (inner ℂ (applyOperatorToState (B x a) ψ)
   382	        (applyOperatorToState ((A x).effect a)
   383	          (applyOperatorToState (C x a) ψ))).re :=
   384	    funext fun x => Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => hrw x a

    40	          f ((P.m : ℝ) ^ 2 * ε) ((P.m * P.d : ℕ) / (P.q : ℝ)) := by

    45	      q := (2 ^ (2 * n + 1)) ^ 3

    47	      hq := ⟨(2 * n + 1) * 3, ⟨3 * n + 1, by omega⟩, by rw [pow_mul]⟩

     3	/-!
     4	# Expanded line measurements
     5	
     6	For a generalized-Pauli basis `W` and a canonical line, the expanded line
     7	measurement is the convolution of the strategy line measurement with the
     8	projective measurement of one Pauli register whose outcome is the restriction
     9	to that line of the low-degree encoding of the measured basis label. This file
    10	states the three consistency conclusions the source draws for that family,
    11	together with the existential form in which the source states them.
    12	
    13	The argument runs as follows. Restricting a multilinear low-degree encoding to
    14	a line gives a polynomial of degree at most `m*d` in the line parameter, and at
    15	most `d` on an axis-parallel line (`LineMeasurement.Restriction`), whose
    16	partial evaluation at a sampled point obeys the elementary calculus of
    17	`LineMeasurement.Evaluation`.
    18	Coarse-graining the generalized Pauli basis measurement along that restriction
    19	gives the ancillary projectors `tau^{W,line}`, which are symmetric and hence
    20	perfectly self-consistent on an EPR pair (`LineMeasurement.Projector`). Their
    21	convolution with the strategy line measurement is again projective and vanishes
    22	outside the degree-`d` outcomes on an axis line (`LineMeasurement.Expanded`).
    23	Self-consistency of the convolution follows from self-consistency of the
    24	strategy line measurements and the data-processing inequality
    25	(`LineMeasurement.SelfConsistency`). The overlap of an expanded line
    26	measurement with the expanded point effects selected by evaluation at the
    27	sampled point factorizes exactly through the ancillary consistency of
    28	`tau^{W,line}` with `tau^{W,u}` (`LineMeasurement.LinePointOverlap`); the
    29	generic bipartite estimates of `LineMeasurement.BipartiteTransport` carry that
    30	overlap to the two bipartitions of the six registers, giving the
    31	evaluation-class conclusion (`LineMeasurement.EvalClassConsistency`) and, by
    32	projective refinement, the line-versus-point conclusion
    33	(`LineMeasurement.LinePointConsistency`).
    34	
    35	Two features of this route differ from the source. The source derives its third
    36	item from its second; here the evaluation-class estimate comes first, from the
    37	exact overlap identity, and the second item follows from it by projective
    38	refinement, so that the source's elementary sub-measurement inequality is not

# Mathematical Language Guidelines

MIPStarRE Lean names and documentation should be written for readers comparing
the formalization with the paper and blueprint.

This is a project-local supplement to the Mathlib-derived documentation,
naming, and style guides in the lean-conventions skill's `MATHLIB_doc`,
`MATHLIB_naming`, and `MATHLIB_style` references.

## Scope

These guidelines apply to:

- public Lean declaration names and namespace names;
- module docstrings;
- declaration docstrings;
- documentation-visible section comments;
- explanatory comments that describe the mathematical role of a declaration.
- blueprint prose and formalization-support notes;
- issue titles and issue bodies;
- PR titles and PR descriptions.

## Source of Truth

Use terminology from the following sources, in this order:

1. `references/ldt-paper/`
2. `blueprint/src/chapter/`
3. established local conventions in nearby Lean files

When the paper has a term for the object, use that term. For Section 5, for
example, prefer orthogonalization lemma, truncation function, rounding to
projectors, rank reduction, and completing to measurement.

## Reference Notation And Terminology

The notation and terminology of the original reference are the default for
reader-facing mathematical text.  A reader should be able to compare a Lean
docstring, blueprint paragraph, issue, or PR description with the cited source
without first learning a private vocabulary used by the formalization.

When Lean must use a different name or representation, define the deviation in a
location which future readers can find from the affected statement.  Use the
first applicable location in the following order:

1. the declaration docstring of the public object whose name or representation
   differs from the paper;
2. the module docstring of the defining Lean file, when the deviation concerns a
   family of declarations in that file;
3. the relevant blueprint paragraph, when the notation appears only in the
   blueprint;
4. a report under `docs/reports/` or `docs/paper-gaps/`, when the deviation is a
   larger discrepancy between the paper, blueprint, and Lean.

The explanation should say:

- the notation or term used in the paper;
- the Lean object or name which represents it;
- the mathematical reason for the difference, if there is one;
- the scope in which the replacement should be used.

A PR description may mention the deviation, but it should not be the only place
where future readers can learn it.

Formalization-only auxiliary lemmas should be introduced as such.  Their prose
should name the nearby paper equation, theorem, or construction they support,
rather than presenting the auxiliary name as paper terminology.

## Naming Norm

Names and prose should describe the mathematical object, hypothesis, or
conclusion. They should not encode the history of how the formalization was
assembled.

Avoid presenting words such as `pipeline`, `wrapper`, `package`, `raw`,
`oneShot`, or `liveBlock` as mathematical terminology unless the cited source
uses them with that meaning. Likewise, avoid implementation-local substitutes
such as `projectivization` or `spectral truncation` when the paper gives a
clearer phrase.

This is a general rule for the repository, not only a rule for file splits.
Module names, namespace names, public declarations, theorem fields, docstrings,
blueprint-facing names, issue titles, and spec documents should name the
mathematical layer under discussion, not the local workflow step, paper line
number, or implementation history.

### Concrete examples

The table below illustrates the naming norm with examples patterned on the
codebase and on names seen during review.  Some entries are existing names;
others are proposed names for future refactors.  The "avoid" column lists
process-shaped names that encode the history of how the formalization was
assembled; the "prefer" column lists mathematical names that a reader of the
paper or blueprint would recognize.

| Avoid (process-shaped)                        | Prefer (mathematical)                     | Rationale                                              |
|:----------------------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------|
| `Line130`                                     | `ProjectiveConsistency`                   | Paper Lemma 5.13, not "the line-130 identity"          |
| `Line169`                                     | `CompletionTransport`                     | Paper Lemma 5.16, step that transports completed data  |
| `Step6`                                       | `Orthonormalization`                      | Paper Section 5, the orthonormalization construction   |
| `FinalAssembly`                               | `DiagonalCompletion`                      | Paper Lemma 5.17, constructing a diagonal POVM         |
| `OneShotIneq`                                 | `SelfConsistencyDataProcessing` (or existing module `Preliminaries.SelfConsistency.DataProcessing`)           | Paper's data-processing inequality for self-consistency |
| `PipelineCheck`                               | `ErrorPropagationBound` (proposed)                   | The bound that propagates error through the test       |
| `QxpLayerWrapper`                             | `ProjectivePOVMCompletion` (proposed)                | The construction from round-projectors to POVMs        |
| `RawSpectralTruncation`                       | `SpectralTruncation`                      | The paper's spectral truncation, not an "unwrapped" version |
| `AddInUStep3To5`                              | `AddInUUpperExcessMass` (proposed)                  | Paper Addendum in §U, the upper excess-mass estimate   |
| `AddInUStep12`                                | `AddInUCommutationTail` (proposed)                   | Paper Addendum in §U, the commutation tail estimate    |

An avoided name is acceptable only when the cited paper itself uses that
phrase as the mathematical name (e.g., a lemma the paper calls "Step 2").
In that case the docstring should cite the paper's phrasing.

File-split PRs are a common place where this rule matters: new leaves should be
named by the mathematical boundary they isolate, and any public declarations
exposed by the split should be reviewed under the same standard.

### Shared helpers

When the same (or nearly the same) helper declaration appears in two or
more chapter-local leaves, the copies should be consolidated into a single
shared helper in an appropriate common module.  This avoids duplication and
ensures that fixes, generalizations, or upstream replacements apply to all
call sites at once.  Issue [#1145] tracks this work across the repository.

Procedure:

1. **Confirm equivalence.**  Compare the statement of each copy.  If the
   types differ only by a chapter-specific parameterization (e.g.,
   `SubMeas (Polynomial params) ι` vs `SubMeas (Point params) ι`),
   parameterize the shared helper over that type via a `variable` or
   explicit argument.
2. **Find the right home.**  Prefer a module that is already imported by
   both call sites.  Typical candidates:
   - `MIPStarRE/LDT/Basic/` for parameter-free operators and bounds,
   - `MIPStarRE/LDT/Preliminaries/` for polynomial/field/character lemmas,
   - The highest chapter that is a common dependency of the two sites.
3. **Name mathematically.**  Give the shared helper a name that describes
   what it states, not which chapter it originally came from.
4. **Replace call sites.**  Delete the chapter-local copies and replace
   their uses with the shared helper.  A thin wrapper is allowed only when it
   preserves a paper-facing or blueprint-facing name that external readers
   need to search for; such wrappers should have a docstring or compatibility
   comment explaining why the alias exists.  Remove the wrapper once that
   paper-facing name is no longer needed for external reference.
5. **Document.**  Add a docstring to the shared helper citing the paper or
   blueprint location it supports.

### Legacy identifier treatment

If a docstring must mention a legacy Lean identifier, cite it in backticks and
describe the mathematical object in paper terminology. If an old public
identifier cannot be renamed in the current PR, record the required migration
in the issue, PR description, or an audit file under `audits/`.

Do not add an empty pass-through abbreviation merely to introduce a second
public name.  This is different from a documented public wrapper allowed in the
shared-helper procedure above: a wrapper must preserve a paper-facing or
blueprint-facing term and must say why the alias exists.

## Review Checklist

Reviewers should use this checklist when examining public names and
documentation prose.  Flag any item that fails.

- [ ] **Naming.**  Do public declaration names, namespace names, module names,
      theorem field names, and docstring prose describe a mathematical object,
      hypothesis, or conclusion?  Or do they encode the history of how the
      formalization was assembled (paper line numbers, workflow steps,
      implementation-phase labels)?
- [ ] **Source alignment.**  For the mathematical content under review, does
      the prose use the terminology in `references/ldt-paper/` or the
      blueprint?  Are process words such as `pipeline`, `wrapper`, `package`,
      `raw`, `oneShot`, or `liveBlock` used as mathematical terms when the
      source does not use them that way?
- [ ] **Deviation documented.**  If a Lean name or representation differs from
      the paper, is the deviation documented in a declaration docstring,
      module docstring, blueprint paragraph, or `docs/paper-gaps/` note, in
      that order of preference?
- [ ] **Auxiliary lemmas.**  Are formalization-only auxiliary lemmas introduced
      as such, with prose naming the nearby paper equation, theorem, or
      construction they support?
- [ ] **Shared helpers.**  Does the PR introduce a helper that already exists
      (or near-exists) in another chapter-local leaf?  If so, has it been
      consolidated into a common module with a mathematical name?
- [ ] **Legacy IDs.**  If a legacy Lean identifier is mentioned, is the
      mathematical object described in paper terminology?  If an old public
      identifier cannot be renamed yet, is the required migration recorded in
      the issue, PR description, or an audit file?
- [ ] **Pass-through names.**  Does the PR add an empty pass-through
      abbreviation that introduces a second public name without adding
      mathematical content?  Reject it unless it is a documented compatibility
      wrapper preserving paper-facing or blueprint-facing terminology.

Review-fix PRs touching a surface covered by an active audit should read the
relevant audit before changing names or prose.

import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.Lines.NondegeneratePastingMass

/-!
# Nondegenerate-line pasting distribution

This module constructs the proof-only normalized product line-point law whose
first sampled line has nonzero direction.

## References

The conditioning supports the pasting argument in `lem:qld-xz-lines`,
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:950-963`, using
the normalized question laws from
`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:504-525`.
-/

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open MIPStarRE.LDT

noncomputable section

/-- The first-line nondegeneracy event has positive mass under the product
line-point law. -/
theorem prod_linePointDist_nondegenerate_mass_pos (L : LdParams) :
    0 < ∑ samples ∈
        (Distribution.prod (linePointDist L) (linePointDist L)).support.filter
          (fun samples => samples.1.1.direction ≠ 0),
      (Distribution.prod (linePointDist L) (linePointDist L)).weight samples := by
  change 0 < nondegenerateLinePastingMass L
  exact lt_of_lt_of_le (by norm_num) (nondegenerateLinePastingMass_bounds L).1

/-- Proof-only question law obtained by conditioning the product line-point law
on nonzero first-line direction and relabeling the two samples for pasting. -/
def nondegenerateLinePastingDist (L : LdParams) :
    Distribution (((LineDesc L × LineDesc L) ×
      (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L))) ×
        (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L))) :=
  (Distribution.restrict (Distribution.prod (linePointDist L) (linePointDist L))
    (fun samples => samples.1.1.direction ≠ 0)
    (prod_linePointDist_nondegenerate_mass_pos L)).map
      (fun samples => (((samples.1.1, samples.2.1), samples.2), samples.1))

/-- The proof-only nondegenerate pasting question law is normalized. -/
theorem nondegenerateLinePastingDist_isProbability (L : LdParams) :
    (nondegenerateLinePastingDist L).IsProbability := by
  exact (Distribution.restrict_isProbability _ _
    (prod_linePointDist_nondegenerate_mass_pos L)).map _

end

end MIPStarRE.QPBT
import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.Lines.RestrictedAverage
import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.Lines.ZeroDirectionMass

/-!
# Retained mass for nondegenerate-line pasting

This module defines the mass retained when the first line in the product
line-point law is restricted to nonzero direction and proves uniform lower and
upper bounds for that mass.

## References

The restriction is the proof-only conditioning used in `lem:qld-xz-lines`,
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:950-963`.
-/

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open MIPStarRE.LDT

noncomputable section

/-- Probability retained by the proof-only first-line nondegeneracy
restriction in the pasting argument for `lem:qld-xz-lines`. -/
def nondegenerateLinePastingMass (L : LdParams) : ℝ :=
  ∑ samples ∈
      (Distribution.prod (linePointDist L) (linePointDist L)).support.filter
        (fun samples => samples.1.1.direction ≠ 0),
    (Distribution.prod (linePointDist L) (linePointDist L)).weight samples

/-- The retained product-law mass lies between one half and one. -/
theorem nondegenerateLinePastingMass_bounds (L : LdParams) :
    1 / 2 ≤ nondegenerateLinePastingMass L ∧
      nondegenerateLinePastingMass L ≤ 1 := by
  classical
  let indicator := fun sample : LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) =>
    if sample.1.direction ≠ 0 then (1 : ℝ) else 0
  have hmass : nondegenerateLinePastingMass L =
      avgOver (linePointDist L) indicator := by
    unfold nondegenerateLinePastingMass
    rw [Distribution.sum_filter_weight_eq_avgOver, avgOver_prod]
    change avgOver (linePointDist L) (fun sample =>
      avgOver (linePointDist L) (fun _ => indicator sample)) = _
    simp_rw [avgOver_const_of_isProbability _ (linePointDist_isProbability L)]
  have haxis : avgOver (aLinePointDist L) indicator = 1 := by
    have hindicator : indicator = fun sample =>
        1 - if sample.1.direction = 0 then (1 : ℝ) else 0 := by
      funext sample
      by_cases hzero : sample.1.direction = 0 <;> simp [indicator, hzero]
    rw [hindicator, avgOver_sub,
      avgOver_const_of_isProbability _ (aLinePointDist_isProbability L),
      aLinePointDist_zero_direction_mass]
    norm_num
  have hdiag : 0 ≤ avgOver (dLinePointDist L) indicator :=
    avgOver_nonneg _ _ fun sample => by
      by_cases hzero : sample.1.direction = 0 <;> simp [indicator, hzero]
  have hlower : 1 / 2 ≤ avgOver (linePointDist L) indicator := by
    rw [linePointDist, avgOver_mix, haxis]
    norm_num
    linarith
  rw [hmass]
  refine ⟨hlower, ?_⟩
  calc
    avgOver (linePointDist L) indicator ≤
      avgOver (linePointDist L) (fun _ => 1) :=
      avgOver_mono _ _ _ fun sample => by
        by_cases hzero : sample.1.direction = 0 <;> simp [indicator, hzero]
    _ = 1 := avgOver_const_of_isProbability _ (linePointDist_isProbability L) 1

end

end MIPStarRE.QPBT

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open MIPStarRE.LDT

noncomputable section

/-- The concrete nondegenerate line-pasting distribution satisfies the
conditional collision bound required by `lem:pasting`. This is the
formalization-only Schwartz--Zippel conditioning auxiliary used in
`lem:qld-xz-lines`, paper lines 950--963. -/
theorem nondegenerateLinePastingDist_collision_bound
    (P : AdmissibleParams) (bound : ℕ) :
    HasConditionalCollisionBound (nondegenerateLinePastingDist P.toLdParams)
      (fun (poly : DegPoly P.toLdParams bound) sample => evalOpt sample.1 sample.2 poly)
      ((bound : ℝ) / Fintype.card (ScalarQ P.toLdParams)) := by
  classical
  let L := P.toLdParams
  apply collision_bound_of_fiber_averages
  intro fixed first second hne
  simp only [nondegenerateLinePastingDist, Distribution.avgOver_map]
  have hpos := prod_linePointDist_nondegenerate_mass_pos L
  apply (mul_le_mul_iff_right₀ hpos).mp
  rw [avgOver_restrict_mul_mass, mul_left_comm _ ((bound : ℝ) /
    Fintype.card (ScalarQ L)), avgOver_restrict_mul_mass]
  have h := prod_linePointDist_nondegenerate_weighted_collision_le
    (fun line sample => if ((line, sample.1), sample) = fixed then 1 else 0)
    (fun line sample => by split_ifs <;> norm_num) first second hne
  have hswap (condition other : Prop) [Decidable condition] [Decidable other] (value : ℝ) :
      (if condition then (if other then value else 0) else 0) =
        (if other then (if condition then value else 0) else 0) := by
    split_ifs <;> rfl
  simpa only [avgOver, Finset.sum_filter, mul_ite, mul_one, mul_zero,
    ite_mul, one_mul, zero_mul, hswap] using h

end

end MIPStarRE.QPBT

+import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.Lines.NondegeneratePastingMass
+
+/-!
+# Nondegenerate-line pasting distribution
+
+This module constructs the proof-only normalized product line-point law whose
+first sampled line has nonzero direction.
+
+## References
+
+The conditioning supports the pasting argument in `lem:qld-xz-lines`,
+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:950-963`, using
+the normalized question laws from
+`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:504-525`.
+-/
+
+namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
+
+open MIPStarRE.LDT
+
+noncomputable section
+
+/-- The first-line nondegeneracy event has positive mass under the product
+line-point law. -/
+theorem prod_linePointDist_nondegenerate_mass_pos (L : LdParams) :
+    0 < ∑ samples ∈
+        (Distribution.prod (linePointDist L) (linePointDist L)).support.filter
+          (fun samples => samples.1.1.direction ≠ 0),
+      (Distribution.prod (linePointDist L) (linePointDist L)).weight samples := by
+  change 0 < nondegenerateLinePastingMass L
+  exact lt_of_lt_of_le (by norm_num) (nondegenerateLinePastingMass_bounds L).1
+
+/-- Proof-only question law obtained by conditioning the product line-point law
+on nonzero first-line direction and relabeling the two samples for pasting. -/
+def nondegenerateLinePastingDist (L : LdParams) :
+    Distribution (((LineDesc L × LineDesc L) ×
+      (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L))) ×
+        (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L))) :=
+  (Distribution.restrict (Distribution.prod (linePointDist L) (linePointDist L))
+    (fun samples => samples.1.1.direction ≠ 0)
+    (prod_linePointDist_nondegenerate_mass_pos L)).map
+      (fun samples => (((samples.1.1, samples.2.1), samples.2), samples.1))
+
+/-- The proof-only nondegenerate pasting question law is normalized. -/
+theorem nondegenerateLinePastingDist_isProbability (L : LdParams) :
+    (nondegenerateLinePastingDist L).IsProbability := by
+  exact (Distribution.restrict_isProbability _ _
+    (prod_linePointDist_nondegenerate_mass_pos L)).map _
+
+end
+
+end MIPStarRE.QPBT

+import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.Lines.RestrictedAverage
+import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.Lines.ZeroDirectionMass
+
+/-!
+# Retained mass for nondegenerate-line pasting
+
+This module defines the mass retained when the first line in the product
+line-point law is restricted to nonzero direction and proves uniform lower and
+upper bounds for that mass.
+
+## References
+
+The restriction is the proof-only conditioning used in `lem:qld-xz-lines`,
+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:950-963`.
+-/
+
+namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
+
+open MIPStarRE.LDT
+
+noncomputable section
+
+/-- Probability retained by the proof-only first-line nondegeneracy
+restriction in the pasting argument for `lem:qld-xz-lines`. -/
+def nondegenerateLinePastingMass (L : LdParams) : ℝ :=
+  ∑ samples ∈
+      (Distribution.prod (linePointDist L) (linePointDist L)).support.filter
+        (fun samples => samples.1.1.direction ≠ 0),
+    (Distribution.prod (linePointDist L) (linePointDist L)).weight samples
+
+/-- The retained product-law mass lies between one half and one. -/
+theorem nondegenerateLinePastingMass_bounds (L : LdParams) :
+    1 / 2 ≤ nondegenerateLinePastingMass L ∧
+      nondegenerateLinePastingMass L ≤ 1 := by
+  classical
+  let indicator := fun sample : LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) =>
+    if sample.1.direction ≠ 0 then (1 : ℝ) else 0
+  have hmass : nondegenerateLinePastingMass L =
+      avgOver (linePointDist L) indicator := by
+    unfold nondegenerateLinePastingMass
+    rw [Distribution.sum_filter_weight_eq_avgOver, avgOver_prod]
+    change avgOver (linePointDist L) (fun sample =>
+      avgOver (linePointDist L) (fun _ => indicator sample)) = _
+    simp_rw [avgOver_const_of_isProbability _ (linePointDist_isProbability L)]
+  have haxis : avgOver (aLinePointDist L) indicator = 1 := by
+    have hindicator : indicator = fun sample =>
+        1 - if sample.1.direction = 0 then (1 : ℝ) else 0 := by
+      funext sample
+      by_cases hzero : sample.1.direction = 0 <;> simp [indicator, hzero]
+    rw [hindicator, avgOver_sub,
+      avgOver_const_of_isProbability _ (aLinePointDist_isProbability L),
+      aLinePointDist_zero_direction_mass]
+    norm_num
+  have hdiag : 0 ≤ avgOver (dLinePointDist L) indicator :=
+    avgOver_nonneg _ _ fun sample => by
+      by_cases hzero : sample.1.direction = 0 <;> simp [indicator, hzero]
+  have hlower : 1 / 2 ≤ avgOver (linePointDist L) indicator := by
+    rw [linePointDist, avgOver_mix, haxis]
+    norm_num
+    linarith
+  rw [hmass]
+  refine ⟨hlower, ?_⟩
+  calc
+    avgOver (linePointDist L) indicator ≤
+      avgOver (linePointDist L) (fun _ => 1) :=
+      avgOver_mono _ _ _ fun sample => by
+        by_cases hzero : sample.1.direction = 0 <;> simp [indicator, hzero]
+    _ = 1 := avgOver_const_of_isProbability _ (linePointDist_isProbability L) 1
+
+end
+
+end MIPStarRE.QPBT

 	$R^{x,z}_{a,b}=M^{Z,z}_b M^{X,x}_a M^{Z,z}_b$.
 	Field-valued approximate commutation bounds its distance from the ordered
 	point product. Point self-consistency and the same commutation estimate
 	bound its off-diagonal overlap across opposite placements.

 \section{Combined line measurements}
 
 \begin{lemma}[Formalization support for coefficient polynomial agreement]
 	\label{lem:coefficient-polynomial-agreement}
 	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.evalCoefficient_collision_card_le}
 	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.linePolynomialOfCoefficients_eq_ofFn,
 		MIPStarRE.QPBT.linePolynomialOfCoefficients_eval,
 		MIPStarRE.QPBT.linePolynomialOfCoefficients_injective,
 		MIPStarRE.QPBT.linePolynomialOfCoefficients_natDegree_le}
 	\leanok
 	Let $K$ be a finite integral domain, let $c\in\N$, and let
 	$f,g\in K^{c+1}$ be distinct coefficient vectors. Their polynomials
 	$p_f(T)=\sum_{i=0}^{c}f_iT^i$ and $p_g(T)=\sum_{i=0}^{c}g_iT^i$
 	agree at at most $c$ elements of $K$.
 	The coefficient representation is injective, preserves evaluation,
 	and has natural degree at most $c$.
 	This is a formalization-only auxiliary for the Schwartz--Zippel step
 	in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-xz-lines}
 	(\texttt{14\_analysis\_of\_the\_pauli\_basis\_test.tex:955}).
 	There is no restriction $c<|K|$.
 \end{lemma}
 \begin{proof}
 	\leanok
 	The coefficient representation is injective, preserves evaluation,
 	and gives polynomials of degree at most $c$. If the polynomials agreed
 	at more than $c$ elements, the univariate root bound applied to their
 	difference would force them to be equal, contradicting $f\ne g$.
 \end{proof}
 
+\begin{lemma}[Formalization support for affine evaluation on a nondegenerate line]
+	\label{lem:nondegenerate-affine-evaluation}
+	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.evalOpt_affine_parameter_of_direction_ne_zero}
+	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.polynomial_ofFn_eval_eq_evalCoefficient}
+	\leanok
+	\uses{def:line, def:ideg-deg-polynomials}
+	Let $\ell \subseteq \F_q^m$ be a line with base point $b$ and direction
+	$v \ne 0$, and let $f$ be a polynomial of degree at most $c$ given by its
+	coefficient vector. For every $t \in \F_q$ the evaluation of $f$ at the
+	point $b + tv$ of $\ell$ is defined and equals
+	$\sum_{i=0}^{c} f_i t^i$. The same coefficient convention agrees with
+	evaluation of the univariate polynomial having those coefficients.
+	This is a formalization-only auxiliary for the Schwartz--Zippel step in
+	the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-xz-lines}
+	(\texttt{14\_analysis\_of\_the\_pauli\_basis\_test.tex:950--955}).
+\end{lemma}
+\begin{proof}
+	\leanok
+	A nonzero direction determines the affine parameter of a point of $\ell$
+	uniquely: if $b + tv = b + sv$ then $(t-s)v = 0$, hence $t = s$. Therefore
+	the evaluation at $b + tv$ is the value of the coefficient polynomial at
+	$t$. The second identity expands the polynomial as a sum of monomials.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Formalization support for affine parameter resampling]
+	\label{lem:line-point-parameter-resampling}
+	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.avgOver_uniform_lineRepMap_resample_parameter}
+	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.avgOver_aLinePointDist_resample_parameter,
+		MIPStarRE.QPBT.avgOver_dLinePointDist_resample_parameter,
+		MIPStarRE.QPBT.avgOver_linePointDist_resample_parameter}
+	\leanok
+	\uses{def:line-point-dist}
+	Let $F$ be a real-valued function of a line and a point of $\F_q^m$, and
+	write $b_\ell$ and $v_\ell$ for the base point and the direction of a line
+	$\ell$. Then
+	\[
+		\E_{(\ell,x)} F(\ell,x)
+		= \E_{(\ell,x)} \E_{t} F(\ell, b_\ell + t v_\ell),
+	\]
+	where $(\ell,x)$ is drawn from the line-point distribution
+	(Definition~\ref{def:line-point-dist}) and $t$ is uniform on $\F_q$. The
+	identity holds separately for the axis-parallel and the diagonal component
+	of that mixture, with no restriction on the direction.
+\end{lemma}
+\begin{proof}
+	\leanok
+	For a uniformly distributed point $x$ and a fixed direction $v$, the
+	canonical representative of the coset $x + \F_q v$ is unchanged by
+	translation along $v$, and $x$ is uniform on that coset. Hence replacing
+	$x$ by the representative shifted by an independent uniform $t$ leaves the
+	joint law of the pair unchanged; this gives the axis-parallel and the
+	diagonal case, and for a zero direction both sides coincide. The
+	line-point identity is the corresponding convex combination of the two.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Formalization support for weighted collision mass on nondegenerate lines]
+	\label{lem:nondegenerate-weighted-line-collision}
+	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.evalOpt_uniform_parameter_collision_le}
+	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.linePointDist_nondegenerate_weighted_collision_le}
+	\leanok
+	\uses{def:line-point-dist, def:ideg-deg-polynomials}
+	Let $f \ne g$ be polynomials of degree at most $c$ on a line $\ell$ with
+	direction $v \ne 0$. Under a uniform affine parameter $t$ on $\F_q$,
+	\[
+		\Pr_{t}\bigl[f(b_\ell + t v) = g(b_\ell + t v)\bigr] \le \frac{c}{q}.
+	\]
+	Consequently, for every weight $w$ on lines with $w(\ell) \ge 0$ for all
+	$\ell$,
+	\[
+		\E_{(\ell,x)}\bigl[\bone{v_\ell \ne 0}\, w(\ell)\,
+			\bone{f(x) = g(x)}\bigr]
+		\le \frac{c}{q}\,
+			\E_{(\ell,x)}\bigl[\bone{v_\ell \ne 0}\, w(\ell)\bigr],
+	\]
+	the expectation being over the line-point distribution
+	(Definition~\ref{def:line-point-dist}). The restriction to nonzero
+	directions is part of the assertion: the corresponding unrestricted
+	inequality is false for the degenerate fibers of that mixture.
+	This is a formalization-only auxiliary for the Schwartz--Zippel step in
+	the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-xz-lines}
+	(\texttt{14\_analysis\_of\_the\_pauli\_basis\_test.tex:950--955}).
+\end{lemma}
+\begin{proof}
+	\leanok
+	\uses{lem:coefficient-polynomial-agreement,
+		lem:nondegenerate-affine-evaluation,
+		lem:line-point-parameter-resampling}
+	By Lemma~\ref{lem:nondegenerate-affine-evaluation} the two evaluations
+	along $\ell$ are the values of the coefficient polynomials of $f$ and $g$
+	at $t$, and by Lemma~\ref{lem:coefficient-polynomial-agreement} these
+	agree for at most $c$ of the $q$ values of $t$, which gives the first
+	bound. For the second, resample the point by an independent uniform affine
+	parameter using Lemma~\ref{lem:line-point-parameter-resampling}, and apply
+	the first bound fiberwise, multiplied by the nonnegative weight; on
+	fibers with zero direction both integrands vanish.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Formalization support for collision mass on a fixed nondegenerate line]
+	\label{lem:nondegenerate-fiber-line-collision}
+	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.linePointDist_nondegenerate_fiber_collision_le}
+	\leanok
+	\uses{def:line-point-dist, def:ideg-deg-polynomials}
+	Let $\ell_0$ be a line of $\F_q^m$ with direction $v_{\ell_0} \ne 0$ and
+	let $f \ne g$ be polynomials of degree at most $c$. Then
+	\[
+		\E_{(\ell,x)}\bigl[\bone{\ell = \ell_0}\,\bone{f(x) = g(x)}\bigr]
+		\le \frac{c}{q}\,
+			\E_{(\ell,x)}\bigl[\bone{\ell = \ell_0}\bigr],
+	\]
+	the expectation being over the line-point distribution
+	(Definition~\ref{def:line-point-dist}). Both sides are unnormalized
+	masses; when the fiber mass on the right is positive, dividing by it gives
+	the conditional collision probability at most $c/q$ that
+	Lemma~\ref{lem:pasting} takes as its hypothesis with $\eta = c/q$. The
+	nonzero-direction hypothesis on $\ell_0$ is part of the assertion.
+	This is a formalization-only auxiliary for the Schwartz--Zippel step in
+	the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-xz-lines}
+	(\texttt{14\_analysis\_of\_the\_pauli\_basis\_test.tex:950--955}); the
+	transport to the product law and to the register presentation of the
+	pasting lemma is separate.
+\end{lemma}
+\begin{proof}
+	\leanok
+	\uses{lem:nondegenerate-weighted-line-collision}
+	Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:nondegenerate-weighted-line-collision} with the
+	nonnegative weight $w(\ell) = \bone{\ell = \ell_0}$. Since
+	$v_{\ell_0} \ne 0$, the indicator $\bone{v_\ell \ne 0}$ is redundant
+	against $\bone{\ell = \ell_0}$ on both sides, which turns the weighted
+	inequality into the stated one.
+\end{proof}
+
 \begin{lemma}[Combined line measurements]
 	\label{lem:qld-xz-lines}
 	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.CombinedLinesWitness}

 	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.ProjectiveSetting.combinedLineMeasurement_axis_degree_X}
 	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.ProjectiveSetting.combinedLineMeasurement_axis_degree_Z}

 	and $f_W$ does not have degree at most $d$, then
 	$T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}=0$.
 \end{lemma}
 \begin{proof}
 	\leanok
 	\uses{def:concrete-paired-line-measurement, def:expanded-line-measurement}

 \begin{lemma}[Consistency of the constructed paired-line measurement]
 	\label{lem:combined-line-measurement-consistency}

 	\uses{lem:qld-4-10, lem:qld-comm-line-cons, lem:pasting,
 		def:concrete-paired-line-measurement, def:consistency}
 	This is a Lean-only construction obligation. Fix a polynomially small
 	function $\delta_Q(\eps)$. There is a function
 	$\delta_P(\eps,md/q)=\poly(\eps,md/q)$, in the corrected sum sense,
 	such that for every projective strategy passing with error $\eps$ and
 	every joint point family satisfying the conclusions of
 	Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-10} with error $\delta_Q(\eps)$, the concrete POVM

 		=\hat M^{(\mathrm{Line},X),\ell_X}_{f_X}

 	after $\delta_Q$ and its polynomial bound. This isolates the consistency
 	part of the preceding construction while retaining its defining
 	measurement; see \cite{gap:qpbt_subline-claims-line-marginal}.

1	import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.Lines.NondegeneratePastingMass
     2	
     3	/-!
     4	# Nondegenerate-line pasting distribution
     5	
     6	This module constructs the proof-only normalized product line-point law whose
     7	first sampled line has nonzero direction.
     8	
     9	## References
    10	
    11	The conditioning supports the pasting argument in `lem:qld-xz-lines`,
    12	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:950-963`, using
    13	the normalized question laws from
    14	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:504-525`.
    15	-/
    16	
    17	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    18	
    19	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    20	
    21	noncomputable section
    22	
    23	/-- The first-line nondegeneracy event has positive mass under the product
    24	line-point law. -/
    25	theorem prod_linePointDist_nondegenerate_mass_pos (L : LdParams) :
    26	    0 < ∑ samples ∈
    27	        (Distribution.prod (linePointDist L) (linePointDist L)).support.filter
    28	          (fun samples => samples.1.1.direction ≠ 0),
    29	      (Distribution.prod (linePointDist L) (linePointDist L)).weight samples := by
    30	  change 0 < nondegenerateLinePastingMass L
    31	  exact lt_of_lt_of_le (by norm_num) (nondegenerateLinePastingMass_bounds L).1
    32	
    33	/-- Proof-only question law obtained by conditioning the product line-point law
    34	on nonzero first-line direction and relabeling the two samples for pasting. -/
    35	def nondegenerateLinePastingDist (L : LdParams) :
    36	    Distribution (((LineDesc L × LineDesc L) ×
    37	      (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L))) ×
    38	        (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L))) :=
    39	  (Distribution.restrict (Distribution.prod (linePointDist L) (linePointDist L))
    40	    (fun samples => samples.1.1.direction ≠ 0)
    41	    (prod_linePointDist_nondegenerate_mass_pos L)).map
    42	      (fun samples => (((samples.1.1, samples.2.1), samples.2), samples.1))
    43	
    44	/-- The proof-only nondegenerate pasting question law is normalized. -/
    45	theorem nondegenerateLinePastingDist_isProbability (L : LdParams) :
    46	    (nondegenerateLinePastingDist L).IsProbability := by
    47	  exact (Distribution.restrict_isProbability _ _
    48	    (prod_linePointDist_nondegenerate_mass_pos L)).map _
    49	
    50	end
    51	
    52	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     4	/-!
     5	# Answer polynomials of the combined strategy
     6	
     7	The combined strategy of `def:ld-combined-strategy` answers every question of
     8	the directly indexed low-degree game at the combined parameters by measuring a
     9	single question of the original game and relabelling its outcome.  Four of its
    10	five cases produce a line answer, that is a bounded coefficient vector, from a
    11	line answer or from a point answer of the original game.  This module collects
    12	the univariate polynomials underlying those relabellings, with their degree

    15	Line answers of both games are bounded coefficient vectors evaluated by
    16	`evalCoefficient`.  The polynomials below are therefore built from
    17	`linePolynomialOfCoefficients` and converted back to coefficient vectors by
    18	`coefficientsOfPolynomial`; the degree bounds are what makes that round trip

    21	The parameter `s` in the two line cases is the affine shift relating the two
    22	canonical parametrizations of the line.

    25	
    26	* `coefficientsOfPolynomial` — the bounded coefficient vector of a polynomial.

    29	* `combinedDiagonalPolynomial` — case 4 of `def:ld-combined-strategy`.
    30	* `fiberLinePolynomial` — cases 3 and 5 of `def:ld-combined-strategy`, the two

    32

 \section{Applying the classical low-degree test}
 \label{sec:apply-ldt}
 
 The combined point and line measurements of the previous two sections are next
 merged into a single measurement returning a pair of global polynomials that
 encode the $X$-basis and the $Z$-basis information simultaneously. This is

## Findings

- [ ] F4 (changes) `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Defs.lean:43` — “coordinate plumbing” is software-engineering language rather than a mathematical description.

## Review

**F1:** The blueprint contains no entries for `nondegenerateLinePastingMass`, `nondegenerateLinePastingMass_bounds`, `prod_linePointDist_nondegenerate_mass_pos`, `nondegenerateLinePastingDist`, or `nondegenerateLinePastingDist_isProbability`. Add separate formalization-support definitions and lemmas near `lem:qld-xz-lines`, with exact statements, `\lean{...}`, `\leanok`, and accurate `\uses`. These entries must remain separate from source `lem:qld-xz-lines`, whose independent, unconditioned product law is different and whose `\notready` remains appropriate.

**F2:** Replace “Lean-only construction obligation” with “formalization-only construction obligation.” Likewise replace “Lean proof” with “formal proof” at `ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:1863`, and “conditional Lean-only result” with “conditional auxiliary result” at `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1403`. The same terminology occurs in added Lean docstrings such as `AnyStrategySoundness.lean:31`, `Lines.lean:51`, `PointErrorObstruction.lean:28`, `GroundCompression.lean:11`, and `Heterogeneous.lean:223`.

**F3:** Rename the public `SubLineRaw`, `subLineRawDist`, `subLineRawDist_isProbability`, `exists_raw_of_mem_subLineDist_support`, and `subLineBranchRaw_map_*` family using the mathematical role already given by the docstrings, for example `SubLineAuxiliarySample`, `subLineAuxiliaryDist`, and `exists_auxiliarySample_of_mem_subLineDist_support`.

**F4:** Replace “formalization-only coordinate plumbing” with “formalization-only coordinate decomposition” or “the coordinate equivalence used by the combining map.”

**F5:** Replace “agree at at most” with “agree at most” or “agree at no more than.”

The remaining changed `\leanok` markers match completed, source-faithful or explicitly scope-restricted declarations. The retained source-facing `\notready` markers remain justified by open obligations or conditional witness inputs.
